did_you_know.text: Psalm 99 opens with a declaration of God’s kingship: when He reigns, the nations tremble and the earth shakes. The verse also describes Him as seated above the cherubim.
The Lord is described as great in Zion and exalted above all the nations, emphasizing both His presence in Zion and His supremacy over all humanity.
The proper response to the Lord’s great and awesome name is praise, and the reason is repeated in the verse: “He is holy.”
The Lord’s kingship is expressed not only through power but also through His love of justice. The verse connects fairness, justice, and righteousness with His rule in Jacob.
The call, “Exalt the Lord our God and worship at His footstool,” combines spiritual exaltation with bowing before the Lord; “His footstool” is an image of a place of honor and presence.
Moses, Aaron, and Samuel are mentioned together as figures who called on the Lord’s name, and the verse presents them as people whose prayers were answered.
According to the psalm, the Lord spoke to Moses, Aaron, and Samuel from the pillar of cloud; it also says that they kept His testimonies and the law He gave them.
The verse presents two aspects of the Lord’s rule: He bears with and forgives, yet He also avenges wrongdoing. In this way, mercy and moral accountability are emphasized together.
The psalm concludes by repeating the call to exalt and worship, this time at the Lord’s holy mountain, and summarizes once more: “Holy is the Lord our God.”
